rubrics.rubric: Does the submission provide exactly the two requested OLCC work products?
criterion: The submission includes a recommendation memo for the licensing manager and enforcement supervisor.
The submission includes a first-90-days inspection and compliance checklist for field staff if the license is issued.
Both deliverables are written as operational internal work products rather than as a generic summary of the PDFs.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo make one clear licensing recommendation for the exact Sportsman Tavern application under review?
criterion: The memo identifies the applicant as IWAS, LLC, dba Sportsman Tavern, at 145 S Redwood Hwy, Cave Junction, Oregon.
The memo identifies the pending application as a Full On-Premises Sales, Commercial license.
The memo chooses exactly one path: issue as a restricted F-COM, request additional follow-up before issuance, or deny.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately describe the July 2025 refusal basis and settlement posture?
criterion: The memo states that the refusal basis is ORS 471.313(1)(e), history of serious and persistent problems at the premises or involving patrons in the immediate vicinity related to alcohol service.
The memo states that the applicant admitted the facts in the notice and that OLCC has a basis to deny the application.

The memo notes that the settlement resolves only the noticed denial basis and that any issued license would carry restrictions, while OLCC may still deny the license or impose additional restrictions based on other facts.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately summarize the same-premises history that created the refusal basis?
criterion: The memo states that the premises history included 16 serious incidents from June 9, 2021 through February 26, 2022.
The memo notes that the OLCC investigation followed a double fatality DUII and that most of the documented incidents involved DUII arrests.

The memo identifies at least two specific charged problems from the 2023 matter, chosen from after-hours alcohol service during the Governor's Executive Order, sale of alcohol to a minor and a juvenile, permitting minors on a #1 minor-posted premises, or use of an employee without a valid service permit.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo acknowledge that the premises risk record continued after the 2023 settlement rather than ending with the 2021-2022 incident cluster?
criterion: The memo states that five administrative violations occurred under the previous licensee between March 19, 2023 and April 14, 2024.
The memo uses those later violations as part of the current risk assessment instead of relying only on the 2021-2022 incident history.
The memo does not imply that a temporary period without documented incidents fully resolved the same-premises eligibility concern.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo use the February 2023 settlement accurately when assessing premises risk?
criterion: The memo states that OLCC originally proposed license cancellation in the 2023 Sportsman Tavern case.
The memo states that the 2023 case was resolved through suspension or civil penalty terms plus license restrictions instead of immediate cancellation.

The memo recognizes that earlier control measures included early closure, drink restrictions, measured pours, and age-verification or surveillance-related controls rather than treating the prior settlement as a simple warning.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately identify the 2025 control measures and restrictions that are meant to overcome the refusal basis?
criterion: The memo discusses the reduced hours restrictions: no alcohol sales or service from 12:00 am to 7:00 am and no patron possession or consumption from 12:30 am to 7:00 am.
The memo discusses the one-container rule, direct-to-patron service requirement, container size caps, and one-ounce measured pours for distilled spirits.

The memo discusses immediate reporting of violent or illegal activity and the video surveillance requirement covering all controlled areas plus the adjacent outdoor area and parking lot, with 30-day retention and 72-hour production.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo squarely address whether this applicant overcomes the same-premises history?
criterion: The memo weighs the severe 2021-2022 history and the later 2023-2024 administrative violations against the new applicant's control plan and agreed restrictions.
The memo addresses the significance of the fact that the 2025 proposed restrictions substantially overlap with controls previously imposed or used at this premises.
The final recommendation is consistent with the evidence and risk logic the memo cites.

rubrics.rubric: Does the restriction checklist operationalize the drink-limit and pour-control restrictions?
criterion: The checklist tells inspectors to verify that a patron is not sold, served, or holding more than one container of alcohol at one time.

The checklist tells inspectors to verify the size caps of 16 ounces of malt beverage, 16 ounces of cider, 6 ounces of wine, and 2 ounces of distilled spirits, and to verify direct service to the patron receiving the drink.
The checklist tells inspectors to verify that distilled spirits are poured using a one-ounce jigger or one-ounce measured liquor bottle pourer.

rubrics.rubric: Does the standard F-COM portion of the checklist cover the food-service requirements that still apply if the license is issued?
criterion: The checklist states that at least five different meals must be available at all times and in all areas where alcoholic beverage service is available.

The checklist states that the premises must have at least 30 qualifying dining seats during a period lasting at least two hours before 10:00 pm unless the Commission determines the premises has a clearly dominant food-service emphasis.
The checklist translates those rules into inspection evidence such as current menu availability, kitchen operations, service-area coverage, and qualifying seating.

rubrics.rubric: Does the standard F-COM portion of the checklist cover lawful alcohol sourcing and related ordinary compliance checks?
criterion: The checklist states that malt beverages, wine, and cider must be obtained from Oregon manufacturers or wholesalers or from out-of-state businesses holding an OLCC direct-to-retailer permit.
The checklist states that distilled liquor must be obtained from an OLCC Retail Liquor Store.
The checklist translates sourcing compliance into inspection evidence such as invoices, delivery records, purchase records, or product-source review.
